note: Rewritten from the original description by Silvestri (1914); the original is in Latin; the nominotypical subspecies was described on the same day as the species, and the measurements follow those of the holotype description; only the soldier and worker are described; the measurement unit mm follows the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The nominotypical subspecies is the typical form described by Silvestri 1914, with the type locality Transvaal, Pretoria. It is closely related to C. truncatus but smaller in body size; it differs greatly from C. bilobatus in body size and in the shape of the labrum. The other subspecies, C. pretorianus heidelbergi, was described by Fuller (1925).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 6 mm; head length 1.63 mm, width 1.30 mm; mandible length 1.43 mm; antenna length 1.82 mm; hind tibia 1.10 mm. Head length about 1/4 greater than width, posterior corners rounded, sides nearly parallel; middle of the labrum wide and deeply concave, the inner side of the anterior angles rounded and the outer side nearly pointed; mandibles slightly longer than head width; antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 almost twice as long as segment 3.
